subject.title: after_tool_call hook receives a flattened string, not the structured ToolResult — plugins cannot detect exec/bash failures

question: Should OpenClaw normalize Codex-native `after_tool_call` results into an OpenClaw-owned structured envelope even when Codex native PostToolUse supplies shell output as a flat string, and where should raw output remain available?
rationale: This is a public plugin-facing payload contract and the current code has two plausible sources of truth: Codex's stable native hook `tool_response` and OpenClaw's app-server item model with structured command status.

options.title: Normalize with raw-output preservation
options.body: Expose a consistent structured outcome for Codex-native tools while keeping the original text in an additive field so existing string consumers have a migration path.

options.title: Preserve Codex payload verbatim
options.body: Keep forwarding Codex `tool_response` unchanged and document that native shell `after_tool_call.result` may be a flat string without exit status.

options.title: Add a parallel details field
options.body: Leave `event.result` untouched but add a documented `resultDetails` or equivalent field for status, exitCode, error, and duration.

recommendation.title: Normalize with raw-output preservation
recommendation.body: Expose a consistent structured outcome for Codex-native tools while keeping the original text in an additive field so existing string consumers have a migration path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main relay and app-server projection code that need the contract decision are attributed to steipete in blame and PR metadata.
